applies_why: The judge evaluates the challenger's covenant-origin analogy, a multi-verse chain, against the Matthew 1:20 link.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: I weighed whether 'the sentence's own words state' is an improper verse-by-verse test or a direct-support note within a chain-vs-chain assessment.
why: The judge expressly treats the challenger's analogy as footed and refers to the defender's chain in CR3 Link 2, so it does not reject the pressed chain merely because no single verse states the contrary.
